findings: NON-BLOCKER: Postgres Float[] round-trip changes the last significant digit (~1e-16 relative; e.g. 0.47140452079103173 → 0.4714045207910317). Exact vector equality across a DB round trip is not achievable; semantic behavior is unaffected (cosine similarity ≈ 1.0). The shipped smoke script only asserts dimension equality, which is consistent with this. Red-team suite asserts max-delta < 1e-12 instead.

NON-BLOCKER: hybridScore's dim-mismatch early return (tagScore) executes before its outcome-0 guards, so a dim-mismatched negative-outcome row can return a positive tagScore from hybridScore directly. Every production recall path goes through recallHybrid, whose suppressedKeys set zeroes negative-outcome rows regardless (proven end-to-end by rt3). No reachable regression.

NON-BLOCKER: no shipped unit test asserts embedding store/skip specifically for the recordHumanDecision leg (its integration test predates the change and does not inspect the embedding column). The QA lane covers this via rt8 (integration, 256-dim stored) and the shared safeEmbed unit tests; the skip-on-failure path for this leg relies on the same proven safeEmbed contract.

NON-BLOCKER: backfill-domain-embeddings.ts change is comment-only; verified base commit a95cc66 already used resolveEmbedder(), so the new comment documents actual behavior (stale-comment fix, not a mismatch).
